theme: कर्म और संन्यास: समभाव से मुक्ति / Action and renunciation: liberation through balance
context: Arjuna asks which path is superior: abandoning action or engaging in selfless action. Krishna answers that both can lead to liberation, but a true renunciant is one who is free from attachment and aversion, not merely one who withdraws from outer duties.
contextHindi: अर्जुन पूछते हैं कि कर्म का त्याग श्रेष्ठ है या निष्काम कर्म? कृष्ण कहते हैं कि दोनों मार्ग मोक्ष तक ले जाते हैं, पर असली संन्यासी वह है जो लगाव और द्वेष से मुक्त है, केवल बाहरी व्यवहार से नहीं।
sanskritDevanagari:
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति |
निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ||५-३||
transliteration:
jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati .
nirdvandvo hi mahābāho sukhaṃ bandhātpramucyate ||5-3||

wordByWord.meaning: He should be known; recognized as such in the inner sense.
The one whose renunciation is constant, not just an external change in activity.
Hates, dislikes, or turns away in aversion.
Desires, longs for, or grasps after.
Free from the pairs of opposites such as pleasure-pain, gain-loss, praise-blame.
From bondage; from the entanglement of craving and ego.

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक सच्चे संन्यासी की पहचान बहुत साफ़ करता है. कृष्ण कहते हैं, 'जिसे जानना चाहिए, वह नित्यसंन्यासी है, जो न द्वेष करे, न इच्छा करे.' यानी वह मन की तरफ़ से भी खाली है. न तो किसी चीज़ से घृणा, न किसी चीज़ को पाने की इच्छा. और यह सिर्फ़ बाहरी जीवन शैली नहीं है; यह आंतरिक स्थिति है. जब मन द्वन्द्व से मुक्त होता है, तब बंधन से आसानी से छुटकारा मिलता है. ध्यान रखना, यह श्लोक 'काम करना छोड़ दो' का संदेश नहीं देता. बल्कि कहता है कि कर्मों के फल में आसक्ति छोड़ दो, मन को ठहराओ, अपने को अपने अहंकार से अलग देखो. तब कर्म भी बंधन नहीं बनता. अगर हम हर चीज़ में 'मैं चाहता हूँ' और 'मैं इसे नहीं चाहता' का खेल समझ लें, तो मन लगातार जकड़ा रहता है. संन्यास का अर्थ है अटैचमेंट से मुक्ति, न कि निष्क्रियता. यही कारण है कि कृष्ण योग को नित्यसंन्यास की ओर ले जाते हैं.
clearEnglish: Here Krishna defines the inward quality of true renunciation. A person is not a real renunciant merely because they stop acting or withdraw socially. A true renunciant is one who neither hates nor longs for, because the mind no longer lives in the oscillation between aversion and grasping. In this verse, the inner state matters more than the outer appearance. The phrase nirdvandva is crucial: it means freedom from pairs of opposites—pleasure and pain, success and failure, attraction and repulsion. When the mind is no longer driven by these polarities, bondage loosens. This is not a call to passivity or moral indifference. It is a call to self-knowledge and detachment from the ego’s cravings. The practical point is that we can act without making action our identity. Even while living in the world, a steady mind can remain free from the binds of desire, fear, and resentment. That is the deeper renunciation Krishna is pointing to.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Text
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states the defining marks of the nityasaṃnyāsin: no hatred, no craving, and freedom from duality. This is an inner criterion, not merely a social role or external vow.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Commentary
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The Divine Life Society commentary says that renunciation is not merely giving up actions because of laziness, ignorance, family quarrel, calamity, or unemployment. It describes true renunciation as freedom from attachment and aversion, and from egoism and desires—not simply physical renunciation of objects.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Inference
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A person can remain active and still be inwardly free. The heart of renunciation is non-ownership of action and non-attachment to results, not abandoning responsibility by default.

practicalApplication.label: Observe the pull
practicalApplication.text: When a task, opinion, or outcome triggers strong dislike or craving, pause and ask: 'Am I reacting from attachment or from clarity?'

practicalApplication.label: Release the ego in ordinary choices
practicalApplication.text: Try doing a small duty without silently narrating 'I did this for myself' or 'I deserve this.' Let the action be service, not self-claiming.

reflectionQuestion: When do I confuse outer withdrawal with inner freedom, and how can I recognize true detachment in my daily reactions?
reflectionQuestionHindi: मैं कब बाहरी अलगाव को आंतरिक स्वतंत्रता समझ लेता हूँ, और अपने दैनिक प्रतिक्रियाओं में सच्चा विराग पहचानने के लिए क्या करना होगा?
